companies.name: COTES
companies.notes: Danish manufacturer of industrial dehumidification systems for battery dry room applications. Key supplier for electrode and cell manufacturing environments.

research.summary: COTES is a Danish manufacturer of industrial dehumidification systems specialising in battery dry room atmosphere conditioning. Their Ultradry and Exergic Technology® systems achieve ultra-low dew points (-40 to -80°C) required for electrode and cell manufacturing, with claimed energy savings of up to 92% versus conventional units. Recent installations at European gigafactories report up to 85% dry-room energy reduction, and Beyonder in Norway has adopted Cotes Ultradry for its battery production line.

companies.name: FOM Technologies
companies.notes: Danish manufacturer of slot-die coating equipment for battery electrode research and production. R&D and pilot-scale coating systems.

research.summary: FOM Technologies is a Danish DTU spin-off producing slot-die coating equipment for battery electrode manufacturing at lab and pilot scale. Their systems offer microliter-level slurry dosage control for uniform electrode layers, used primarily in R&D and scale-up applications. In 2025–2026 the company partnered with Honeywell to integrate its slot-die technology into an AI-powered battery manufacturing platform at the University of Alabama's AMP Center (scheduled Q2 2026).

companies.name: AWL
companies.notes: AWL-Techniek, Netherlands. Welding automation systems for battery cell, module, and pack assembly.

research.summary: AWL-Techniek (Netherlands) is a system integrator specialising in welding automation for battery cell, module, and pack assembly. Their solutions use laser welding and thermally conductive adhesive bonding for battery module production, with full automation of module handling, sorting, fixing, and connection. The company has branches in the Netherlands, Czech Republic, China, Mexico, USA, and UK, serving major EV battery manufacturers globally.

companies.name: SPARKNANO
companies.notes: Spin-off from TU/e (Eindhoven). Atomic layer deposition (ALD) systems for battery electrode coating, enabling uniform nano-scale coatings for improved cell performance.

research.summary: SparkNano (TU/e spin-off, Netherlands) develops spatial atomic layer deposition (ALD) equipment for battery electrode coating at industrial scale. In 2025 the company unveiled the SparkNano Omega™, the world's first high-speed roll-to-roll spatial ALD system capable of web speeds up to 100 m/min and widths up to 1.5 m, enabling nanoscale LiF and other protective coatings on anode and cathode foils with claimed 10% improvement in capacity retention. The system operates at atmospheric pressure, targeting high-volume Li-ion battery production.

companies.name: PEC
companies.notes: PEC (Precision Equipment Company), Belgian manufacturer of battery formation, aging, and testing equipment. Key supplier for cell finishing in battery gigafactories.

research.summary: PEC N.V. (Belgium) is a world-leading supplier of cell finishing equipment — formation, aging, DCIR/OCV measurement, degassing, grading, and sorting systems — for cylindrical, pouch, and prismatic battery cells. The company has installed turnkey automated cell finishing lines at gigafactories and pilot lines running with leading German OEMs, competing with Chroma ATE and Digatron in the fast-formation equipment segment. PEC's formation towers are a critical step in transitioning cells from assembly to usable product.

research.summary: AGC Inc. AGC has developed proprietary sulfide solid electrolyte production technology by combining its glass and chemicals expertise, targeting mass production for all-solid-state batteries. The company is positioned as a key materials supplier for next-generation battery production rather than a production equipment maker in the conventional sense.

A notable recent development: in March 2025, ACC extended its partnership with EQUANS France to double production capacity at the Billy-Berclau gigafactory by 2026.

companies.name: FISAIR

products.name: atmosphere conditioning / dry room air treatment

companies.notes: FISAIR, Spain. Industrial air treatment systems including dehumidification and dry room solutions for battery electrode and cell manufacturing.

research.summary: FISAIR (Spain) manufactures desiccant dehumidifiers for lithium-ion battery production, supplying atmosphere conditioning equipment for dry rooms where electrode and cell manufacturing require dew points from -40 to -80°C. Their DFLOW range features a dual heat recovery system that reduces energy consumption while maintaining fresh air pressurisation. The company continuously tracks evolving battery chemistries and material changes to adapt their humidity control solutions.

companies.name: LAZPIUR
companies.notes: Talleres Lazpiur, Bergara (Basque Country), Spain. CNC machining centers used in battery manufacturing tooling and precision component production.

research.summary: Lazpiur (Bergara, Basque Country, Spain) manufactures high-precision machining centres and tooling for hot, warm, and cold forming processes, with battery cell components listed among their application areas. The company operates nine CNC lathes and seven 5-axis high-speed palletising machining centres. As a Basque precision engineering firm they serve the automotive and battery tooling supply chain rather than supplying complete battery production lines.

companies.name: COMEXI
companies.notes: COMEXI Group, Girona, Spain. Flexible packaging and coating/converting machinery applicable to battery separator and electrode film production.

research.summary: COMEXI (Girona, Spain) has expanded into battery manufacturing with a dedicated range of high-precision slitters for copper and aluminium electrode foils and battery separator films — the S2 Energy and S4 Energy series. These systems integrate advanced quality assurance with closed-loop control and traceability features. COMEXI differentiates from Asian competitors by offering European-manufactured precision slitting solutions tailored to the electrode converting step.

companies.name: TELSONIC
companies.notes: TELSONIC AG, Bronschhofen, Switzerland. Ultrasonic welding systems for battery tab and busbar welding in cell assembly.

research.summary: TELSONIC AG (Bronschhofen, Switzerland) supplies ultrasonic welding systems for battery cell assembly, primarily used for tab-to-busbar interconnection in EV battery packs. Their SONIQTWIST® torsional and PowerWheel® technologies enable welding of aluminium cell connectors to copper busbars with minimised intermetallic formation and high electrical conductivity. The company's MPX system operates at 20 kHz / 6.5 kW and is widely adopted in European battery module production lines.

companies.notes: Werner Mäder AG, Switzerland. Precision roller and calendering equipment for battery electrode manufacturing.

research.summary: Werner Mäder AG (Switzerland) manufactures precision rollers and calendering systems used in battery electrode densification, a critical step in electrode manufacturing that compresses the coated electrode to the target porosity and thickness. Specific recent contract announcements or European gigafactory deliveries could not be confirmed in public sources, but the company is listed as a recognised European supplier of electrode calendering equipment. The calendering step directly affects electrode energy density and cell performance.

companies.name: BÜHLER
companies.notes: Bühler Group, Uzwil, Switzerland. Mixing and processing equipment including wet grinding and dispersing systems for battery electrode slurry preparation.

research.summary: Bühler Group (Uzwil, Switzerland) is one of the most established European suppliers of continuous electrode slurry mixing systems for lithium-ion battery manufacturing, having delivered over 113 complete systems worldwide as of February 2026. Their continuous mixing process — integrating dosing, pre-mixing, kneading, dispersing, and degassing — reduces slurry energy consumption to 56 kWh/t versus ~200 kWh/t for batch processes. A notable 2025 contract involves delivering four continuous mixing lines to FIB S.p.A. (Italy, 8 GWh capacity) with production starting in 2026.

companies.name: CAMFIL
companies.notes: CAMFIL, Sweden. Industrial air filtration (HEPA, molecular filtration) for battery dry rooms and cleanrooms.

research.summary: Camfil (Sweden) is a leading manufacturer of HEPA and ULPA air filters for battery dry rooms and cleanrooms, providing Megalam panels and molecular filtration systems that meet the ultra-low particulate requirements of lithium-ion battery electrode and cell manufacturing. Their filtration solutions are used throughout battery gigafactory environments to prevent contamination. The cleanroom technology market — of which Camfil is a major part — is valued at $10B+ in 2025 with battery gigafactories as a key growth driver.

companies.name: Quintus Technologies
companies.notes: Quintus Technologies, Västerås, Sweden. Isostatic pressing equipment used in solid-state battery manufacturing and electrode densification.

research.summary: Quintus Technologies (Västerås, Sweden) specialises in isostatic pressing equipment for battery manufacturing, with a growing focus on all-solid-state battery production. In November 2025 the company unveiled the QIB 300 and QIB 600 Warm Isostatic Press series — pilot-scale systems achieving up to 600 MPa / 145°C for ASSB cell densification and bonding. In March 2025 Quintus opened a dedicated Battery Application Center to support developers from testing to scale-up. The company is presenting at Interbattery 2026 on scaling ASSB production with warm isostatic pressing.

companies.name: Munters
companies.notes: Munters, Sweden. Industrial humidity control and dry room solutions critical for lithium-ion electrode and cell manufacturing.

research.summary: Munters (Sweden) is a global leader in industrial humidity control and dry room dehumidification for lithium-ion battery manufacturing. Their Low Dew Point (LDP) dehumidifiers are engineered specifically for battery dry rooms requiring ultra-dry air at low temperatures. In 2025, Munters secured a $30M order from a US heavy/medium-duty vehicle battery cell manufacturer for LDP systems, with delivery scheduled for Q2-Q3 2026. Previous contracts include a dry room system for Morrow Batteries' Arendal gigafactory in Norway.

companies.name: JOT Automation
companies.notes: JOT Automation, Tampere, Finland. Automated assembly and end-of-line testing systems for battery cells and modules.

research.summary: JOT Automation (Oulu, Finland; part of Victory Precision Group) is a world-leading provider of custom test and assembly automation for electronics and EV batteries, present in 11 countries. Their battery solutions include turnkey assembly lines for EV battery systems (unpacking, testing, welding, final-product testing) and a dedicated Battery Test solution for cylindrical, pouch, and prismatic cells. No specific 2025–2026 gigafactory contract announcements were found in public sources.

companies.name: LAHTI Precision
companies.notes: Lahti Precision, Lahti, Finland. Industrial conveyor and handling systems for battery manufacturing lines.

research.summary: Lahti Precision (Lahti, Finland) is a weighing technology and material handling specialist with over 100 years of expertise, serving customers including battery material manufacturers. In March 2023 the company was acquired by Tamtron Group and now operates as Tamtron Precision Oy. Their products cover industrial conveyor belt scales, big bag stations, dispensing systems, and the mScales SaaS material flow management system — relevant for raw material handling in battery active material production.

companies.name: PFEIFFER VACUUM
companies.notes: Pfeiffer Vacuum Technology, Asslar, Germany. Vacuum pumps and systems for battery cell manufacturing including electrolyte filling and degassing.

research.summary: Pfeiffer Vacuum Technology (Asslar, Germany; part of Busch Group) supplies vacuum pumps and leak detection systems for battery cell manufacturing, specifically electrolyte filling (vacuum-assisted wetting at ~0.01 mbar), formation degassing, and cell housing leak testing. At Battery Show Europe 2025 (Stuttgart), Pfeiffer presented the HiScroll 46 scroll pump paired with the ASI 35 tracer gas leak detector, enabling fast high-throughput leak testing of battery cell housings in production lines.

companies.name: AZO
companies.notes: AZO GmbH, Osterburken, Germany. Powder handling, dosing, and conveying systems for battery active material processing in electrode manufacturing.

research.summary: AZO GmbH (Osterburken, Germany) supplies bulk powder handling, dosing, and conveying systems for battery manufacturing, covering both electrode production (handling active materials such as lithium, cobalt, graphite) and battery recycling (sorting recovered powders for re-entry into the supply chain). Their AMIXON mixer dryer reactors and precision sifters handle the specific challenges of battery-grade powders. AZO is also active in supporting dry electrode production trends where precise powder-to-film process control is critical.

companies.name: HORIBA
companies.notes: HORIBA (Japanese), European operations in Germany. Analytical and measurement instruments including particle size analyzers, electrochemical measurement, and emission monitoring used in battery R&D and quality control.

research.summary: HORIBA (Japanese company with major European operations in Germany) provides a comprehensive suite of analytical instruments for battery manufacturing quality control and R&D: particle size analysers (LA-960V2), Raman spectrometers, GD-OES, ICP-OES, and electrochemical measurement systems for cell, module, and pack testing. Their 2025 positioning paper 'Mastering the Battery Journey' covers the full battery value chain from materials characterisation to end-of-life. HORIBA instruments are widely used in electrode manufacturing (particle size of active materials) and cell finishing (EIS, capacity cycling).

A notable recent project: teamtechnik Poland is responsible for supply and installation of a complete battery module production line for Impact Clean Power Technology's GigafactoryX in Pruszków, Poland — the largest teamtechnik Poland implementation, using Bosch Rexroth TS7 conveyor technology for the first time globally.

In 2025 GROB opened a technology centre in Lyon, France, and exhibited at Battery Show Europe. A major in-house exhibition marking the company's 100th anniversary is planned for March 2026 in Mindelheim, showcasing the latest battery production innovations.

Together with the Technology Centre Dresden, KMS has developed coating systems for battery and energy storage production. The company's headquarters is in Waldmössingen, not Schönau im Schwarzwald as previously noted.

companies.name: MANZ

open_questions: Manz AG filed for insolvency in early 2025 and Tesla Automation GmbH agreed to purchase the site — confirm current operational status and whether battery equipment business continues under new ownership

companies.notes: Manz AG, Reutlingen, Germany. Full-line battery manufacturing equipment: electrode coating, cell stacking/winding, formation and testing. One of the most complete battery equipment providers in Europe. Filed for insolvency Feb 2025; Tesla Automation GmbH agreed to purchase the site.

research.summary: Manz AG (Reutlingen, Germany) was one of Europe's most complete battery production equipment providers, covering electrode manufacturing, cell stacking/winding, and cell finishing. In February 2025 the company opened insolvency proceedings following a weakened European battery cell equipment market, and Tesla Automation GmbH agreed to acquire the site. Manz had previously divested its battery cell production equipment business and was refocusing on battery module assembly and industrial automation before the insolvency. The battery equipment brand and assets are now in transition.

companies.name: COHERENT
companies.notes: Coherent Corp. (US), significant European/German operations. Laser systems for battery tab notching, welding, and electrode cutting.

research.summary: Coherent Corp. (US, with major European operations) supplies high-power laser systems for battery cell assembly: electrode foil cutting and notching, tab-to-foil welding, cell housing sealing, and safety valve welding. Their edge welding technology connects aluminium/copper electrode foil stacks to battery tabs with precise laser control. Coherent's laser systems are used in the cell assembly step across pouch, prismatic, and cylindrical battery production lines.

companies.name: IKA
companies.notes: IKA-Werke GmbH, Staufen im Breisgau, Germany. Laboratory and industrial mixing, stirring, and heating equipment for battery electrode slurry preparation and R&D.

research.summary: IKA-Werke GmbH (Staufen im Breisgau, Germany) supplies mixing, dispersing, and heating equipment for battery electrode slurry preparation at both lab and industrial scale, with claimed productivity improvements of up to 15% versus conventional mixers. In 2025 IKA expanded its partnership with Dec Group to offer integrated powder handling and mixing solutions for battery production. The company also launched enhanced dry electrode processing solutions in 2025, positioning for the solvent-free electrode manufacturing trend.

companies.name: VON ARDENNE
companies.notes: VON ARDENNE GmbH, Dresden, Germany. Vacuum coating and plasma processing systems for battery electrode coating and solid-state electrolyte deposition.

research.summary: VON ARDENNE GmbH (Dresden, Germany) is a technology leader in vacuum coating systems for next-generation battery cell components, supplying equipment for solid-state electrolyte deposition, corrosion protection layers, and lithophilic coatings for anode-free battery concepts. The company recently commissioned the OPTA X300 deposition tool in a new cleanroom. At H2 & FC EXPO 2026 (Tokyo), VON ARDENNE presented the X-CONDUCT carbon coating and the VICA900 coating system for fuel cell and battery applications.

companies.name: SCHMID

open_questions: Clarify whether SCHMID's role in this map is specifically for Li-ion electrode surface treatment or for redox flow battery production — SCHMID Pekintaş is building a vanadium redox flow battery gigafactory in Turkey

companies.notes: SCHMID Group, Freudenstadt, Germany. Surface treatment and wet processing equipment for battery electrode and cell manufacturing.

research.summary: SCHMID Group (Freudenstadt, Germany) is known for precision wet processing and surface treatment equipment, with a strong base in PCB and advanced packaging manufacturing. In the battery sector SCHMID is active primarily through flow battery systems — SCHMID Pekintaş is targeting redox flow battery cost reduction with a planned Turkish gigafactory. In March 2026 SCHMID also secured a major order for wet-process production equipment for AI/HPC infrastructure. The company's role as a Li-ion battery equipment supplier specifically requires further confirmation.

companies.name: EIRICH
companies.notes: Maschinenfabrik Gustav Eirich GmbH, Hardheim, Germany. Intensive mixers and granulation systems for battery active material and electrode slurry preparation.

research.summary: Maschinenfabrik Gustav Eirich (Hardheim, Germany) supplies intensive mixers (including the MixSolver® variant) for battery electrode slurry and dry electrode compound preparation, supporting wet, semi-dry, and dry processes. At Battery Show Europe (May 2025, Stuttgart) Eirich presented a 500-litre mixer RLV12W Vac, laboratory mixers C5, and the new El1nano for solid-state battery development (up to 100 ml). Eirich mixers offer significantly lower energy consumption and higher homogenisation than conventional planetary mixers.

companies.name: Brabender
companies.notes: Brabender GmbH, Duisburg, Germany. Process measurement instruments and laboratory mixing/extrusion equipment for battery material characterization.

research.summary: Brabender GmbH (Duisburg, Germany; now part of Anton Paar as Anton Paar TorqueTec GmbH) supplies torque rheometers, measuring kneaders, and twin-screw extruders used for battery electrode material characterisation and process development, including testing extrudability and rheology of anode and cathode compounds. The company has 25 years of collaboration with IKTS Dresden and Hermsdorf using their equipment for battery electrode compound development. Brabender exhibits at Battery Power Conference 2025 and 2026.

companies.name: Jonas & Redmann
companies.notes: Jonas & Redmann Group, Berlin, Germany. Specialized battery manufacturing systems: stacking, winding, tab welding, and complete cell assembly lines. One of Germany's primary battery equipment specialists.

research.summary: Jonas & Redmann (Berlin, Germany) is one of Germany's primary specialists in battery cell and module assembly equipment, supplying systems for electrode stacking, winding, laser processing, tab welding, and complete cell assembly lines from R&D to mass production scale. The company has a strategic cooperation agreement with Liebherr-Verzahntechnik for combined automation system offerings. Jonas & Redmann exhibits at RE+ 2025 (North American solar and energy storage trade show) and participates in German research initiatives on battery cell stacking innovation.

companies.name: COLLIN
companies.notes: Dr. Collin GmbH, Ebersberg, Germany (now COLLIN Lab & Pilot Solutions GmbH, Maitenbeth). Film and foil extrusion systems for battery separator and electrode film production.

research.summary: COLLIN Lab & Pilot Solutions GmbH (Maitenbeth, Germany; formerly Dr. Collin) manufactures film and foil extrusion lines, roll mills, and slot-die coating heads for battery separator and electrode film production. Their machines handle electrode coating onto foil (including solvent-free NMP-free processes), separator film extrusion, and calendering of thin electrode films. The company exhibited at K 2025 (Düsseldorf) and has been active in battery manufacturing equipment since a milestone pilot line installation in 1999.

companies.name: ABB
companies.notes: ABB Ltd (Swiss-Swedish multinational). Industrial robots, drives, and automation systems widely used in battery module and pack assembly lines. Listed in Germany column but pan-European presence.

research.summary: ABB Robotics (Swiss-Swedish, global operations) supplies industrial robots, cobots, drives, and turnkey automation solutions for battery cell, module, and pack assembly. ABB delivered robots to Scania's new battery assembly plant in Sweden and partnered with Gotion High-Tech for gigafactory automation in Europe and the US. ABB released new large robot models in 2025 specifically targeting EV battery material handling, increasing speed and flexibility for gigafactory floor operations.

companies.name: FFT
companies.notes: FFT Produktionssysteme GmbH & Co. KG (Fulda, Germany). Flexible factory systems for EV and battery pack/cell assembly, electrolyte filling, and mini-environment integration.

research.summary: FFT Produktionssysteme (Fulda, Germany; partner of Siemens) designs and builds turnkey automated production systems for battery manufacturing including electrolyte filling, cell housing sealing, BOL/EOL battery testing, and flexible (dis)assembly lines for battery recycling. FFT announced the first battery cell from the FFB PreFab facility on December 15, 2025, marking a milestone in German battery manufacturing. The company also develops mini-environment systems that isolate critical battery processes to reduce dry-room energy costs by 25–40%.

companies.name: Leybold
companies.notes: Leybold GmbH, Cologne, Germany (Atlas Copco subsidiary). Vacuum pumps and systems for battery manufacturing including electrolyte filling and cell degassing.

research.summary: Leybold GmbH (Cologne, Germany; Atlas Copco subsidiary) supplies dry-compressing oil-free vacuum pumps (DRYVAC-LIB, CLAWVAC, VARODRY-LIB) for battery cell manufacturing, covering electrode drying, electrolyte vacuum filling at ≤0.01 mbar, and formation degassing. Their pumps are specifically engineered to handle NMP solvent traces and toxic formation gases safely. Leybold cooperates with battery manufacturers to co-develop tailored vacuum solutions for evolving cell chemistries and formats.

companies.name: jagenberg
companies.notes: Jagenberg Group, Neuss, Germany. Slitting, winding, and roll handling equipment for battery electrode foil and separator processing.

research.summary: Jagenberg Group (Neuss, Germany) supplies precision slitting and winding equipment for battery electrode foil and separator processing through its Jagenberg Converting Solutions (JCS) brand and Kampf portfolio. At Battery Show Europe 2025 (Stuttgart, May 2025) Jagenberg presented the EvoSlitter, TechSlitter CHRO, and MicroSlitter for sensitive electrode and separator foils. The company is also contributing to the European GIGABAT project, developing roll-to-roll infrared drying systems for anode foils targeting commercial deployment by 2027.

companies.name: laserline
companies.notes: Laserline GmbH, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Germany. High-power diode laser systems for battery tab cutting and welding applications.

research.summary: Laserline GmbH (Mülheim an der Ruhr, Germany) manufactures high-power diode laser systems for battery manufacturing, including electrode foil welding, tab cutting, and infrared drying of battery foils in roll-to-roll processes. At Laser World of Photonics 2025 (Munich) the company presented its complete industrial diode laser portfolio including the LDFblue 6000-60 (6 kW, blue wavelength) specifically for copper welding. Laserline's LDM technology enables rapid power adjustment within microseconds for multi-layer electrode tab welding without damaging adjacent separator films.

companies.name: aumann
companies.notes: Aumann AG, Beelen, Germany. Winding technology and assembly automation for battery cells (cylindrical and prismatic) and modules.

research.summary: Aumann AG (Beelen, Germany) is a global leader in coil winding technology and e-mobility assembly automation, supplying winding machines for battery cells and assembly systems for battery modules and packs. In its Q1 2026 earnings, the company confirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of ~€160M and EBITDA margin 6–8%. E-mobility segment revenue fell ~45% in 2024–2025 due to reduced OEM order intake, prompting Aumann to diversify into aerospace, defence, clean tech, and life sciences via its Next Automation division.

companies.name: KUKA
companies.notes: KUKA AG, Augsburg, Germany (Midea Group). Industrial robots and automation systems widely used in battery cell, module, and pack manufacturing lines.

research.summary: KUKA AG (Augsburg, Germany; Midea Group) provides certified cleanroom and dry-room robots for battery cell, module, and pack production including pouch, prismatic, and cylindrical cell formats. A notable 2025 development involves KUKA robots being trialled in 'mini-environment' battery cell production at KIT (Karlsruhe Institute of Technology), where process containment significantly reduces the energy needed to create dry-room conditions. KUKA also supplies complete battery module assembly lines integrating tab welding, module measuring, and housing integration.

companies.name: PINK
companies.notes: PINK GmbH Thermosysteme, Wertheim, Germany. Vacuum lamination and heat press systems used in solid-state battery and pouch cell manufacturing.

research.summary: PINK GmbH Thermosysteme (Wertheim/Main, Germany; 180+ employees) manufactures vacuum drying, sintering, and soldering systems used in battery cell manufacturing. Notable battery contracts include delivery of 30 vacuum furnaces to Britishvolt and a long-term partnership with Cellforce Group / Porsche AG for high-performance solid-state battery manufacturing. PINK exhibited at SEMICON West 2025, confirming ongoing presence in advanced semiconductor and battery manufacturing equipment markets.

companies.name: OLBRICH
companies.notes: Olbrich GmbH, Bocholt, Germany (now part of Matthews Engineering). Coating, laminating, and converting machines for battery electrode and separator production.

research.summary: OLBRICH GmbH (Bocholt, Germany; now operating as Matthews Engineering together with Saueressig and Polytype Converting) specialises in advanced coating and laminating machinery for battery electrode and separator production, including calender systems and roll-to-roll primer coating lines. Since joining Matthews Engineering, their battery energy division has expanded through synergies across the combined portfolio. Olbrich also joined UPCELL, the European Battery Manufacturing Alliance, as a member through Saueressig.

companies.name: ZIMMER Group
companies.notes: ZIMMER Group, Germany. Gripper and clamping technology for battery cell handling in automated assembly lines.

research.summary: ZIMMER Group (Germany) is a specialist in battery cell handling grippers and clamping technology, with over 100,000 development hours in e-mobility solutions since 2014. Their HPM2000 series magnetic grippers for cylindrical cells (65 N holding force) and custom grippers for pouch cells, modules, and high-voltage battery packs are used in automated battery assembly lines. At Automate 2025, ZIMMER debuted the ZiMo flexible robotic cell and new magnetic grippers for cylindrical battery cells.

companies.name: NETZSCH
companies.notes: NETZSCH Group, Selb, Germany. Wet grinding and dispersing equipment for battery active material processing and electrode slurry preparation.

research.summary: NETZSCH Group (Selb, Germany) supplies wet grinding and dispersing equipment for battery active material processing including the PMH planetary mixer and intensive mixers for electrode slurry preparation, reducing mixing time from ~4 hours to 1–2 hours versus conventional planetary mixers. NETZSCH also offers wet grinding systems for silicon-based anode materials (high-capacity next-generation anodes). The company's Application Seminar on Wet Grinding is scheduled for November 2026 in Selb.

companies.name: KROENERT
companies.notes: Kroenert GmbH, Hamburg, Germany. Precision coating and laminating machinery for battery electrode and separator film production.

research.summary: Kroenert GmbH (Hamburg, Germany; founded 1903) manufactures customised coating and laminating machines for web-like materials, with battery electrode and separator membrane production as a major growth application. Their LabCo modular lab machine supports electrode coating and separator coating development. Kroenert exhibited at ICE Europe 2025 showcasing innovations for energy savings and lower emissions in coating processes. Battery electrode coating and separator membrane machinery is cited as a planned major future business area for the company.

companies.name: Zeppelin Systems
companies.notes: Zeppelin Systems GmbH, Germany. Bulk material handling, conveying, and intensive mixing systems for battery active material processing.

research.summary: Zeppelin Systems GmbH (Germany) provides safe and scalable bulk material handling and processing solutions for battery mass production, covering raw material intake, conveying, storage, and precise dosing into calender machines. Their FM intensive mixers support dry and semi-dry electrode compound mixing, including dispersion of nanoparticulate conductive additives for LFP, NCA, NCM, and graphite. Test series have been conducted with customers and research institutions, and the company presented battery solutions at the Batteries Event in Lyon.
